acme-dev: hey @support, we rotated our API key this morning and since then all requests from our app to Redwood return 401 invalid_api_key. curl from my laptop with the same value works fine though. can you help?

tara: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl you ran (sanitized) and how you injected the key into k8s? common culprits: trailing newline, env var quoting, or using the wrong header (Bearer vs Redwood-API-Key). :thinking:

acme-dev: thanks. here's the curl we used locally (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABCdefGhIjKlMnoPqRst" \  
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/respond -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
and in k8s we store the key as a secret and mount it as an env var in the container: `API_KEY` then our app sets header `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`.

mike: quick questions: 1) does the header that works locally exactly match what the pod sends? 2) what's the length of the key inside the pod? you can exec into the pod and run `printf "%s" "$API_KEY" | od -An -t u1 | tr -s ' ' \"\n\"` or simpler `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | wc -c` to check for stray newline/CR.

acme-dev: i did `kubectl exec -it app-123 -- printenv | grep API_KEY` and it printed the key (sanitized), length locally is 32 chars but inside pod `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | wc -c` returns 33. so there's one extra byte.

tara: aha — that's the smoking gun. most likely the secret was created using `echo "${KEY}" | base64` or `echo "..."` which appends a \n. when you base64-decode or otherwise reconstruct, the newline becomes part of the header value and Redwood treats that literally, causing a 401. solution: ensure you use `echo -n` or `printf '%s'`. also when creating k8s secrets from literal, prefer `kubectl create secret generic mykey --from-literal=key="$KEY"`.

acme-dev: interesting. we actually scripted secret creation in CI with `echo $REDWOOD_KEY | base64` -> wrote into YAML. CI runs on Windows runners occasionally; could CRLF be involved?

olivia: yes Windows can introduce CRLF (\r\n). If the key ends up with `\r` the server will see an extra char. You can check for CR with `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | od -c` and look for `\r\n` sequences. Also double-check any YAML editors that wrap long lines.

acme-dev: running `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | od -c` inside pod shows `s k _ l i v e _ A B C d e f G h I j K l M n o P q R s t  \r  \n` so yep there's a \r then \n.

tara: ok that's the bug. quick remediation: update the secret value ensuring no newline/CR. e.g. locally: `printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64 --wrap=0` (Linux) or on mac `printf '%s' "$KEY" | base64` then paste into your secret manifest. or skip base64 roundtrip and do `kubectl create secret generic redwood-key --from-literal=apiKey="$KEY" -n <ns>` from a machine that preserves literal.

mike: for an immediate workaround you can add a pre-start entrypoint in the container to trim whitespace from env var: `export API_KEY="$(echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | tr -d '\\r\\n')"` or in node `process.env.API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY.replace(/[
]+$/,'')`. but better to fix at secret source.

acme-dev: patched the secret in CI (used `printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_KEY" | tr -d '\\r'`) and redeployed — requests now succeed. thank you! :white_check_mark:

support-bot: note added to thread: root cause = CRLF/extra newline in API key from CI secret creation; recommend docs snippet for creating secrets without newlines.

tara: i'll follow up later with a short docs blurb for the KB and a checklist for troubleshooting 401 invalid_api_key (include: header name, header content length, env var checks, base64/echo pitfalls, where to look in CI). thanks for confirming the fix.

acme-dev: would be great — also maybe a small diagnostic endpoint we can hit that returns key length (masked) so we can detect issues automatically.

olivia: good idea — filed an internal ticket to discuss a host-level diagnostic or a support endpoint that returns masked metadata (e.g., length, prefix match). filing number: INT-2026-314.

acme-dev: cheers all, appreciate the fast help.
